pass_b_english: …things belonging to humanity that alone are fitting to the united Word; since indeed the Emmanuel is the one, alone, and true Son, he is understood toward us to be both God and man. "You have subjected all things under his feet."

He begins, he says, with the thoughts toward the construction of man in the beginning and what first became; but he is occupied with how we have been made by God according to his image and likeness, and we have been richly honored, having received to rule over the things upon the earth. Since indeed the beginning of the race, that is, Adam, has grieved the divine commandment, and the human intellect has moreover become very easy toward wrongdoing, by this we are deprived in the world of glory and incorruption and of the good things in the beginning; yet we have been saved through Christ, and by the grace from him we have acquired the things formerly given toward ascension.

The breadth of the following word widens to include such narrations; for the divinely-inspired David has laid down the excess of the day toward us: "What indeed is man," he says, "that you should remember him, or son of man, that you should visit him?" He is small, thus, also and humble, and an animal from the earth. Yet he made him to differ a little from the angels, for we are defeated, as is confessed, of the nature and glory of the holy angels. Not indeed with honor and glory did the God of all things deem worthy and show bright ones; for he has grasped him for a beginning upon the earth and has established him "over the works of his hands."

And the blessed David has indeed marveled appropriately at what is upon us. And the most wise Paul, being a very skilled craftsman in spiritual thoughts, indeed turns wittily toward an explanation of the mystery of the things said, but names the state of the age following this one, and the repetition according to the seasons of the things given to us, or rather their fulfillment. For we have pierced through, as I said, the grace in Adam. For it is indeed said regarding him, as the first in human nature, 'Increase and multiply and have dominion' over it (Gen 1:28); but now he does not say, 'we see all things subjected to him.'

Therefore, let us seek a different time of the matter, according to which it shall be, and the truth of that which is said to us, from being a lie of a God not knowing. He says thus that the inhabited world to come is to be subjected not rather by angels, but that this is to be given to those upon the earth. Since the mystagogues debate concerning the inhabited world coming to us, how could anyone be indifferent? For, turning away from the things having come, they seek to find the things coming, and they advise that one must hasten toward the prize of the higher calling, and they thirst for the hope of the saints, according to which all things will be subjected to them and they will have dominion over the earth.

And the Savior himself was remembering, saying, "Blessed are the gentle, for they themselves shall inherit the earth" (Matt 5:5). Who then is it that through whom the recapitulation of all things concerning us has become from God and the Father? It is evident that it is Christ, which also follows us to say, as through the lyre of the singer, "The Lord is a part of my inheritance and of my cup; you are the one restoring my inheritance to me" (Ps 16:5); for through him we have had the repetition of those good things granted in the beginning according to nature, and the certainty into possession. And it is unceasing to see this in no other way than having been written about it by the divine Paul: "The [one] a little being diminished by angels" we see Jesus through the passion of death "with glory and honor being crowned" (Heb 2:9).

You hear how above all things, the most supreme throne, which is worshiped with the Father by the spirits above in order of God, to whom thousands of thousands of angels serve, and also myriads of myriads stand by, the mystagogue brings down again among us and the manner of approaching the emptying he relates immediately, and whatever through it is made firm to the human nature as good things. Understand indeed being diminished a little…
